summary: Deschutes National Forest summit lookout on Bachelor Butte, now Mount Bachelor: cupola cabin about 1922, replaced 1931, abandoned 1939; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: D-6 cupola cabin (about 1922); replacement cab 1931 (sources differ on type)
facts.status_note: Cab abandoned in 1939 and since removed, per the register and firelookout.com; the inventory gives no removal date. No source describes what remains on the summit.

staffing.status: lookouts named in newspapers 1922-1939; little used from 1939

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Deschutes National Forest

events.note: Newspaper announced a planned summit station; the Deschutes inventory lists a 1917 telephone and observation post
D-6 cupola cabin; register says about 1922, firelookout.com about 1921; June 1922 newspaper reports lumber moving to the summit
J.B. Gauldin, formerly at Pine Mountain, was to be lookout once the station was complete
Ice and storm damage; a forest note called for replacing the building
Cab replaced; inventory says 14 by 14 L-4-31 ground cabin; register says Region-5 cab; firelookout.com says L-4 cab
Damage blamed on climbers; snow and rain warped the floor
Supplies dropped by airplane to the lookout
Register and firelookout.com say abandoned 1939; a Bend paper said the summit was little used
Leland Maker on the summit for three days late in the season

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com lists 4,273 ft; the register gives 9,065 ft (2,763 m) and an 1932 newspaper gives 9,065 feet. The story uses the register figure.
The register says about 1922 and firelookout.com says about 1921; June and July 1922 newspaper reports describe construction. The story uses 1922.
The register says Region-5 cab; firelookout.com and the Deschutes inventory say L-4 (inventory: L-4-31 ground cabin). The story reports the disagreement.
The inventory lists a 1917 telephone and observation post; the 1917 newspaper only announced a planned station. The story reports both.

sources.title: An Inventory of Deschutes County Lookouts

notes_for_editor: The early history and the replacement cab rest on a 2008 personal inventory blog and a compiled newspaper page; the register and firelookout.com agree on the 1939 abandonment and removal but not on the cab type or the date. firelookout.com's 4,273 ft elevation is contradicted by the register and the 1932 newspaper and is treated as an error. Brief record checked: elevation_m 2763.0 matches the register; kind 'ground' is supported for the 1931 cab but the 1922 cupola cabin's placement is not stated; no corrections proposed. Access left out of facts because no source describes access today; Wikipedia's 'ski lifts' route line is the only current-use source. Used one WebSearch and five distinct page reads.
